driver-and-vehicle-administration.purpose: Support alta, baja, editing, assignment, suspension, recovery, and audit for drivers and vehicles through composed management surfaces.
useWhen: Operators manage drivers, vehicles, cards, documents, or assignments.
Rows require status, identity, quick actions, pagination, and audit recovery.
Lifecycle actions need confirmation, permissions, and feedback.
doNotUseWithoutReview: The process is only a static list.
Lifecycle consequences, permissions, or audit policy are unclear.
Driver and vehicle processs are mixed without clear ownership.
foundations: Defines split management layout, table density, summary panels, and action placement.
Owns lifecycle labels, confirmation copy, status, empty states, and audit language.
Controls active, suspended, review, maintenance, and selected states semantically.
Loaded, loading, empty, selected, dirty, suspended, pending, error, and audit states are explicit.
Edit, assignment, and confirmation surfaces use Design System overlays without becoming table components.
Identity, status, actions, pagination, and audit feedback are keyboard reachable and text-backed.
slots: Driver rows composed from Design System table behavior.
Vehicle rows composed from Design System table behavior.
Selected vehicle/card or recent lifecycle event.
Invite, edit, assign, suspend, recover, or export.
Paged datasets and remote result sets.
variants: Driver identity, status, assignment, and lifecycle actions.
Vehicle status, card summary, maintenance state, and assignment action.
Suspended or failed entities show recovery and audit trail.
motion: Selected row updates detail context without page jump.
Confirmation and toast feedback preserve table context.
Page changes preserve toolbar and status orientation.
accessibility: Tables have labels and row context.
Pagination and audit feedback are keyboard reachable.
tests: Driver and vehicle tabs or sections remain distinct.
Lifecycle action requires confirmation when destructive.
Empty and audit states are visible.

canDecide: Use this pattern for driver and vehicle lifecycle processs.
Compose package Table and bounded Package components instead of management-table components.
Use Audit Event for lifecycle evidence.
mustAsk: Lifecycle policy, permissions, data ownership, audit requirements, or recovery rules are unclear.
Actions affect identity, employment, finance, cards, compliance, or legal state.
rejectIf: Lifecycle actions have no confirmation or audit path.
The table is a fake component instead of Design System composition.
miel.handoff: Confirm driver and vehicle lifecycle actions, permissions, row data, assignment rules, audit policy, recovery, and pagination.
